ev.q: approximately 33,000 persons aged > 60 years in the United States were treated in hospital emergency departments
Annualized estimates for this report were based on weighted data for 488 nonfatal physical assault--related injuries
Rates for persons aged 60--69 years (105) were more than two times greater than those for the two older age categories
91.3% of assaulted older adults were treated and released from EDs
a greater proportion of older assault victims were women (43.4% versus 39.1% p = 0.11)
an estimated 33,026 persons aged > 60 years were treated in U.S. hospital EDs for nonfatal assault--related injuries
Compared with persons aged 20--59 years, a greater proportion of older assault victims were women
Rates for persons aged 60--69 years (105) were more than two times greater than those for the two older age categories
CDC analyzed data from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System-All Injury Program

methods_quotes.q: Data from these cases were weighted by the inverse of the probability of selection to provide annualized national estimates
A direct variance estimation procedure was used to calculate 95% confidence intervals and to account for the complex sample design
National estimates might be unstable because they are based on <20 cases or coefficient of variation is >30%.
Rates should be interpreted with caution because of high percentage of unknowns.
